body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Tuesday, October 6, and the story leading the day is a big one for Arvin High School — its Ballet Folklorico program is getting a new dance studio nearly three times the size of its current room. Outside, expect a hot one: a high near 99°, a low around 70° tonight, moderate air quality, and no active weather alerts or fires for Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

Deputies had a busy night across the county, starting with a burglary on Breckenridge Road that ended with a homeowner holding a suspect at gunpoint. According to the Sheriff's Office log, the resident called dispatchers shortly before 11 p.m. to report he had the suspect detained after an earlier break-in at the home. A second suspect ran to a black GMC and left westbound on Breckenridge Road; a neighbor told deputies the truck had turned south on Comanche Drive. Units staged at Breckenridge and Comanche while a patrol car followed the vehicle westbound at normal speeds, and the search through the Comanche Drive foothills carried past midnight before the truck was reported heading south out of the area.

Elsewhere, traffic units were sent at 9:49 p.m. after roughly 50 vehicles moving eastbound on Westside Parkway approaching Calloway Drive. Officers were asked to identify anyone involved and to check Coffee Road at the parkway as the group split, with part of it reported heading toward the Truxtun Avenue off-ramp and Highway 99. Departments were advised to keep units free while the group was tracked through the area.

Fire and medical crews answered several calls overnight. At 9:55 p.m., crews were told a crash had started as a vehicle versus a tree before the vehicle went down into a ravine and came to rest with power lines down nearby; the occupants were out of the vehicle and were reported possibly trying to reach the water, and a second vehicle was reported down at the riverbank a short time later. At 4:28 a.m., a three-vehicle collision was reported in front of a business in the 1100 block of East Truxtun Avenue, with a dark-colored SUV involved and a possible pin-in. Engine 2 and Rescue 2 were on scene and reported the driver out of the vehicle with minor to moderate injuries. At 4:19 a.m., a woman whispering on the phone told dispatchers she was locked inside a car parked in front of a home in the 2500 block of Ledgeview Lane.

Deputies also worked a hit-and-run whose driver ran off on foot, an assault where a man showed a pistol and fled in an SUV, alarms at a District Boulevard business and a Truxtun Avenue building, and a string of medical aids. The rest of the log was disturbances, welfare checks and a handful of fights.

## Today's weather

It's currently 75° at Meadows Field (KBFL), on the way to a high near 99° and a low around 70° tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are reported. Air quality is 65 — moderate — so sensitive groups may want to take it easy during the hottest part of the afternoon. If you're out and about, plan for a genuinely hot October day: shade, water, and a break during the peak hours will go a long way.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that school book bans hit a record high, with a new study finding nearly 12,000 removals.** The figure marks the highest number recorded since researchers began tracking the trend, and it lands as districts across the country — including here in Kern County — continue to weigh which titles belong on library shelves. The study's findings add fresh data to a debate that has played out at local school board meetings for the past several years, with parents and educators on both sides pressing their case.

**According to 23ABC, Arvin High School's Ballet Folklorico program is getting a new dance studio nearly three times bigger than the space students use now.** Teacher Brenda Ruiz told the station the program started with just five students and has grown popular enough that space has become a problem — about 20 students fit in the current room, so the group has to split into smaller sessions. Principal Gabriel Ramirez-Leyva said talks about a larger classroom began last year because of the room's capacity, and the program currently keeps a wait list. The new facility will include dressing rooms, a laundry room and more storage for costumes and shoes. Students got their first look at the room Monday afternoon; senior Noemi Lopez Gonzalez said she can't wait for the remodeling to be finished.

**KGET 17 reports that President Trump has approved death by firing squad for the convicted Fort Hood shooter.** The decision concerns one of the most closely watched military cases in recent memory and is drawing national attention to how the sentence will be carried out. We'll keep an eye on any local reaction in the days ahead.

**KGET 17 also reports that televangelist Jim Bakker, who built the "PTL Club" empire with Tammy Faye Bakker, has died at 86.** Bakker's ministry and later legal troubles made him a fixture of American religious broadcasting for decades, and his death closes a long chapter in that world.

**23ABC reports that President Donald Trump drew criticism from California politicians after remarks about Los Angeles and San Diego during a rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, on Monday.** Trump suggested Iran could "take out" the two cities, calling it "a very small price to pay." San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria responded that his city is "not collateral damage" and "not expendable," while Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass said on X that the president's statements are dangerous and could compromise safety. Governor Gavin Newsom called the remarks "deranged and dangerous."

**According to 23ABC, calls for the release of former Bakersfield resident and Air Force veteran Travis Leake from Russian detention have been renewed as his mother demonstrates in Washington, D.C.** Leake has been held in Russia since June 2023 and is serving a 13-year sentence in a penal colony after being accused of possessing and selling drugs. His mother, Garcia, traveled to the capital Monday hoping to speak with the Trump administration, saying the court records showed no real evidence against her son. Advocate Jon Franks noted that Leake has now been left behind in three successive deals, and in a recorded call Leake said his government has done "absolutely nothing" to help him.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Planet Fitness has acquired Bakersfield's Body Xchange Health Club locations.** The deal reshapes the local gym landscape and means members at those clubs will see the Planet Fitness brand and format going forward. We'll share more details on what it means for memberships as they become available.

## Something good

Arvin High's Ballet Folklorico dancers have something real to celebrate this week. The program that began with five students is getting a dedicated studio nearly three times the size of its current room, complete with dressing rooms, a laundry room and proper storage for costumes and shoes. Students saw the space for the first time Monday, and senior Noemi Lopez Gonzalez summed it up best — looking at the room, she said, it's exciting to know this will be their future practice place.

## Coming up this week

It's a full week of public meetings at Bakersfield City Hall. Wednesday, October 7, starts early with the Police Civil Service Commission at 8:30 a.m. and a special session of the same commission at 8:45 a.m., followed by City Council Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and City Council Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. On Thursday, October 8, the Housing and Community Development Committee meets at noon, and Friday, October 9, brings the Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee, also at noon. Looking ahead to next week, the Special Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee meets Monday, October 12, at noon, and the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets Tuesday, October 13, at noon.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a run of shows lined up. NB RIDAZ brings the "Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off" tour Friday, October 9, followed by FANTASIAS on Saturday, October 10. United We Dance takes the stage Friday, October 16, with the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour on Saturday, October 17, and Fortune Feimster's "Taking Care of Biscuits" comedy tour closing out the stretch on Sunday, October 18. The Fox is also selling season passes for its Cults & Classics series.

Have a good Tuesday, Bakersfield — stay cool out there.

top.title: School book bans hit record high with nearly 12,000 removals, study finds
